Single run per configuration (n=1 per eval). Differences this small are within run-to-run variance; treat as a pilot, not a result.

Non-discriminating: all 17 mechanical assertions (container queries, overflow-wrap, no JS measurement, field-sizing, min/max bounds, resize-y, unchanged form JS, deps unchanged, build ok) passed in BOTH configurations. The baseline model already chose container queries and field-sizing: content unprompted.

The only failed assertion (baseline textarea run) is a verification-process check: no explicit deleted-content test was reported. Evidence for a pass was indirect (a later one-line measurement returned to the minimum height), so this is marginal.

Both runs in each pair independently reached the same support facts (container queries Baseline Widely available; field-sizing Baseline Newly available since June 2026, Chrome 123 / Firefox 152 / Safari 26.2) and cited MDN and Can I use.

Observable skill effects: with-skill runs read all three reference files first (~4 extra tool calls), used the supports-[field-sizing:content]: gate from patterns.md (redundant, since unknown declarations are dropped anyway, as the baseline noted), put @container on a wrapper <li> per the skill's 'an element cannot size-query itself' note (the baseline used @container on the article and queried the inner div, which is equally correct), and checked keyboard focus and contrast, which the baseline card run skipped.

Baseline touches the skill did not produce: lh-unit min/max heights that reproduce the rows=4 height exactly; hyphens-auto and max-w-prose on the card; an explicit note that no @supports gate is needed.

Cost: textarea with-skill used +36k tokens and +228s vs baseline; card with-skill used +2k tokens but finished 128s faster (baseline lost time to a port collision). Net time delta is dominated by environment noise.

Test-harness issue: two concurrent runs bound the same port (8847) and one with-skill run briefly observed the other run's page; outputs were unaffected but future runs should assign distinct ports per run.

Eval design: these two briefs did not discriminate because the baseline model already knows the features. Better discriminators would be the boundary checks in fewer-parts-evaluation.md (Tailwind v3 repo, Safari 15.6 constraint, no-network, small-edit scope, existing carousel with focus management).
